name: Tardive dyskinesia
summary: Tardive dyskinesia is a persistent hyperkinetic movement disorder after dopamine-receptor-blocking agents. Two VMAT2 inhibitors are FDA-labeled for TD in adults: valbenazine (capsules and sprinkle capsules) and deutetrabenazine (twice-daily tablets and once-daily XR tablets). No new TD drugs were approved in 2024–2026; Ingrezza Sprinkle (2024) was a new formulation.
plainSummary: Tardive dyskinesia causes movements a person can't control, often of the mouth, face, or limbs, after long-term use of some psychiatric or stomach medicines. Two daily medicines can reduce these movements.

approved.indication: Treatment of adults with tardive dyskinesia.

dosing.target: 80 mg once daily after 1 week (40 or 60 mg once daily may be considered based on response and tolerability)
dosing.notes: 40 mg once daily for known CYP2D6 poor metabolizers, with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, or in moderate–severe hepatic impairment. Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers. Sprinkle capsules may be opened onto soft food. Can be continued with antipsychotics.

contraindications: History of hypersensitivity to valbenazine or any component
approved.plainSummary: Valbenazine is a once-a-day capsule that can reduce the uncontrolled movements of tardive dyskinesia. The sprinkle version can be opened and mixed into soft food.

verified.note: Checked on the label revised 4/2026. The label's boxed warning (depression and suicidality) applies to the Huntington's chorea indication, not TD. A generic valbenazine ANDA (Zydus) received FDA approval in 2024, but no generic label appears on DailyMed and no US launch was confirmed.

approved.indication: Treatment of tardive dyskinesia in adults.

dosing.start: 12 mg/day (Austedo XR 12 mg once daily, or Austedo 6 mg twice daily with food)
dosing.target: Increase by 6 mg/day at weekly intervals based on TD reduction and tolerability
dosing.notes: Max 36 mg/day in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers or with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Austedo total daily doses ≥12 mg are split twice daily. When switching from tetrabenazine, stop tetrabenazine and start deutetrabenazine the next day.

contraindications: Taking reserpine (wait at least 20 days after stopping)
Taking MAOIs or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI
Huntington's disease with suicidality or untreated/inadequately treated depression
approved.plainSummary: Deutetrabenazine is a pill taken once or twice a day that can reduce the uncontrolled movements of tardive dyskinesia. The dose is raised slowly each week.

verified.note: Checked on the label revised 2/2025. Boxed warning (depression and suicidality) applies to Huntington's disease patients, not the TD indication. Austedo XR was approved in 2023.
